learning_outcomes.text: Students understand the basic concepts of Supply Chain Management (SCM) and can explain the importance of an efficient and integrated supply chain for business success.
Students are able to analyze and critically evaluate the different elements of a Supply Chain to identify weaknesses and potential for improvement.

Students acquire sound knowledge of modern information technologies and IT solutions used in logistics and SCM, including Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), Transport Management Systems (TMS), and Advanced Planning and Scheduling (APS) systems.
Students can compare and select the functions and characteristics of various IT solutions for SCM to meet the specific requirements of a company and its Supply Chain.
Students are able to plan, control, and monitor the implementation of IT solutions into existing Supply Chain processes to ensure a smooth and efficient integration process.
Students are capable of collecting, analyzing, and interpreting data from various sources in the supply chain to make informed decisions and strategic measures for Supply Chain optimization.

Students can understand the importance of real-time information and data for reactive and proactive control of supply chains and assess the integration of IoT and Big Data technologies into SCM processes.
Students recognize the challenges and risks associated with the use of IT solutions in SCM and can propose and implement appropriate security measures and controls to minimize risk.
Students can analyze practical case studies and scenarios where IT solutions have been successfully applied in SCM and apply their insights to develop innovative solutions for real challenges.
Students are able to use their knowledge and acquired skills to design and present a comprehensive concept for the implementation of an IT-supported Supply Chain in a fictitious business scenario.

syllabus_topics: Definition and importance of Supply Chain Management (SCM) in the modern economy
Goals and functions of an efficient Supply Chain for companies
Decisions between in-house production and external sourcing with cooperation possibilities
Development of strategic procurement strategies to ensure goods availability
Different sourcing strategies such as in- and outsourcing, local and global sourcing
New sourcing approaches such as eSourcing and Cooperative Sourcing for efficient supplier management
Identification and evaluation of risks in the Supply Chain
Use of early warning systems for proactive risk prevention and management
Information and material flows between suppliers and customers
Processes from national and international supplier search to supplier evaluation
Environmental and social aspects in the supply chain
Sustainable procurement practices and ethical supplier relationships
Internet of Things (IoT) and its importance for SCM
Automation and digital process optimization in the supply chain
Use of RFID and IoT technologies for tracking goods movements
Big Data analytics for informed decisions and forecasts
Principles of Lean Management in the supply chain
Waste reduction and efficiency improvement
Collaboration along the supply chain for optimized processes
Integration of suppliers and customers into the SCM system
Sustainability and Diversity along the Supply Chain
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
